## Implementation Report — round 1

**Status:** READY-FOR-REVIEW

**Summary.** Forward-pass-only measurement rig for issue #654 (per-layer query
displacement of the context-conditioned residual stream). Added a dual-position
residual extractor + linear CKA to the analysis library, plus a four-script
pipeline (CPU battery build → GPU dual-position extraction → CPU metrics+figures
→ gcp/auto dispatch driver). No training, no checkpoints, no HF model uploads.
All four phases smoke-ran end-to-end; the GPU extraction phase was exercised on
the REAL Qwen-2.5-7B on CPU at N=32 (no local GPU). PASS_UNIFIED smoke.

### (a) What was done
- `src/explore_persona_space/analysis/probes.py`: ADDED
  `extract_dual_position_activations` (plan §3(a)). One forward pass per prompt,
  reads context-end + query-end at every layer via `hs[L+1][0, idx]`,
  `add_special_tokens=False`, batch 1, fp32 CPU — mirrors the existing
  `extract_residual_stream_activations` (which is UNTOUCHED; its signature is
  verified unchanged, so #594/#553/#634 callers keep working). `readout_position`
  param adds the optional companion 3rd-slot read. Asserts
  `0 <= c_idx < q_idx < seq_len` per prompt.
- `src/explore_persona_space/analysis/representation_shift.py`: ADDED
  `linear_cka` (Kornblith 2019 HSIC-Frobenius form, column-center,
  geometric-mean-self-HSIC denominator, fp32→fp64 for invariance stability,
  `n>=2` production assert, `[0,1]` clamp) + `cka_per_layer`.
- `tests/test_linear_cka.py`: NEW. Self-similarity, orthogonal invariance,
  isotropic-scale invariance (+ negative scale), symmetry, independent-Gaussian
  floor, range bounds, `n<2`/mismatched-n raises, `cka_per_layer` shape — 9
  tests, CPU, <8s.
- `scripts/issue654_build_battery.py`: NEW. CPU pre-pod builder. 4 context tiers
  (persona 11 = 10 PERSONAS minus the explicit 4-persona exclusion set +
  ASSISTANT_PROMPT; generic 20 UltraChat first-user; ICL 20 held-out 4-exchange
  UltraChat blocks disjoint from generic + the query bank, hard-asserted;
  wildchat 30 via the #617 loader pulled first, fail-loud) × the frozen 10-query
  bank (3 short on-topic from `EVAL_QUESTIONS[:3]` + 7 frozen new strings).
  Derives `ctx_end_idx` / `query_end_idx` from the ChatML template, hard-asserts
  the prefix invariant (A4) + ordering per pair, prints offset sanity for the
  first 8, writes `battery.json` with meta (exact query strings, persona names,
  sources, ultrachat provenance, git commit).
- `scripts/issue654_extract.py`: NEW. GPU on-pod single-forward dual-position
  extractor. Loads Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct bf16, asserts `num_hidden_layers==28`
  (A1) + `hidden_size==3584` (A2). Per distinct context, a SECOND forward over
  the context-only prompt reads the assistant-gen slot (companion same-position,
  reused across that context's queries). Per pair, re-confirms A4 ordering then
  the dual-position read; atomic per-pair `.pt` writes; `extraction_manifest.json`
  with per-pair offsets + decoded sanity + the >5% offset-fail kill check + model
  config + companion file paths. `--smoke` = one cell (4 contexts × 2 queries),
  identical code path.
- `scripts/issue654_analyze.py`: NEW. CPU off-pod metrics (reads `.pt` banks
  only, no GPU/model). Per layer: centered cosine (per-bank global-mean +
  L2-normalize), raw cosine, B=1000 derangement floor GLOBAL + per-tier
  within-type (2.5/97.5 band), matched-minus-shuffled headline, linear CKA +
  shuffled-bank CKA floor, companion same-position contrast. Writes
  `per_layer_displacement.json` (keyed context_type × layer × query_type) +
  per-cell breakdowns; `--figures` emits 6 PNGs (hero, raw-vs-centered, CKA,
  scatter anchors, violin by query type, companion-vs-two-position) via
  `paper_plots`.
- `scripts/issue654_dispatch.sh`: NEW. gcp/auto driver
  (`REPO_ROOT="$WORKLOAD_ROOT"`), extract phase only, `[phase=...]` logging,
  HF folder-upload of the `.pt` banks + manifest to
  `issue654_query_displacement/analysis_tensors/` with a fresh-listing verify,
  poll_pipeline sentinel (`sentinel_schema_version:1`, `kind:epm:results`,
  `version:1`, note payload), terminal `[phase=done]`. `WANDB_PROJECT` set. No
  `task.py` shellout; CVD pin N/A (single GPU). The CPU analyze phase runs
  OFF-pod (not invoked by the driver), per plan §8.

  batch=1 with explicit per-prompt offsets — "batching > 1 risks position-offset
  bugs across padded batches" and the win is marginal at 891 forwards (<15 min
  GPU). I kept batch=1, matching the plan + the existing

  compares the context-only assistant-gen slot vs the context+query QUERY-END

  per tier — flagged in the analyze docstring. An alternative (reading the SAME
  assistant-gen slot in both context-only and context+query forwards) would need

  finite-sample bias ≈ d/n (Song et al. 2012); at d/n=0.32 the empirical floor
  is ~0.24 (measured across 20 seeds). I kept the plan's named dims with a 0.35
  bound (still cleanly separates from self-similar 1.0) AND added a stricter
  n=1000 sub-0.12 check that hits the plan's intended low-CKA region. Documented

# Adding a user query never pushes the last-token state off its context: context-end vs query-end residual cosine stays 6–25× above the shuffled floor at every layer of Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct (MODERATE confidence)

<!-- clean-result-v3 -->

## Takeaways

- Over all 28 layers and 810 pairs, the query-end residual is **6.2–25× above the shuffled-pair floor** in centered cosine. The "no persistence" null is rejected at every depth.
- Per-pair centered cosine decays **0.60 (layer 0) → 0.088 (layer 27)** — context-dominant early, progressively query-integrated late, but never reaching the floor.
- A confound-free same-slot read (context-only vs context+query) **never drops below ~0.66 cosine** — a full user turn displaces the generation-slot state by at most ~1/3.
- Whole-bank linear CKA does the **opposite**: **0.29 at layer 7** rising to **0.76 at layer 27** — late layers compress contexts toward shared directions as individual pairs drift.
- Context type separates only at layer 0 (a prompt-structure confound); on the same-slot read the four tiers cluster within **~0.07** — no clean "persona persists more" effect (H3 weak).

## What I ran

- **Why:** A recurring question in this project's persona-localization line is *where* in the stack a model stops "being" its context and starts answering the query. Prior work read one position per prompt for family clustering ([#594](https://eps.superkaiba.com/tasks/594)) or role-vs-persona separation ([#634](https://eps.superkaiba.com/tasks/634)); none compared the context-end and query-end positions within the same prompt. This run measures that within-prompt displacement per layer, to characterize context-dominant vs query-dominant layer regimes.
- **Design:** One manipulated axis — **read position** (context-span-end vs query-span-end token) — crossed with context type (4 tiers) × query type (on/off-topic × short/long). 81 contexts × 10 queries = 810 pairs, one forward pass each, residuals read at all 28 layers. Single seed (42).
- **Training:** none — forward-pass measurement only on base `Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct` (bf16, `output_hidden_states=True`, ChatML).
- **Eval:** per-layer per-pair **centered cosine** (global-mean-centered per bank, the anisotropy-robust DV) between the context-end and query-end residuals; a **shuffled-pair derangement floor** (B=1000) for significance; **whole-bank linear CKA** as a secondary geometry read; and a **companion same-position contrast** (context-only vs context+query at the fixed assistant-generation slot) that removes the different-token confound. Raw cosine reported alongside for the anisotropy caveat. No judge, no generation.

## Findings

### Context persistence sits 6–25× above the shuffled floor at every layer (H2 rejected)

Primary DV: per-pair centered cosine between the context-span-end and query-span-end residual, per layer. The shuffled-pair floor (which query pairs with which context, deranged within tier) is the baseline any two different-ending residuals share. If the state just tracked the last few words, matched cosine would sit on this floor (H2).

![Per-tier matched centered cosine vs layer, with shuffled-pair floor bands; matched curves sit far above the near-zero floor at every depth](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/superkaiba/explore-persona-space/92ddfce6bbc78df8675b1747462b1ec1c74b7d6f/figures/issue_654/hero_displacement_blog.png)

> **Figure.** *The query-end state stays nearer its own context than a random one's at every layer.* Solid = matched-pair centered cosine per context tier; shaded = that tier's shuffled-pair floor (2.5/97.5 pctile, B=1000), which hugs zero. Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct, 810 pairs.

- The floor sits at **0.00 ± ~0.01** everywhere; the matched gap above it runs **25× the floor half-band at layer 0 down to a minimum 6.2× at layer 26** (14.5× at layer 27), never inside the band.
- The query-end state is always far closer to *its own* context than to a random one's — real context memory at this position, decisively rejecting H2.

### The depth profile decays smoothly — context-dominant early, query-integrated late (H1)

Reading the matched-minus-shuffled gap as a function of depth answers the regime question the Goal poses.

![Matched-minus-shuffled centered-cosine gap per layer, per tier; all curves largest at layer 0 and decaying with depth toward a tight low-positive cluster](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/superkaiba/explore-persona-space/92ddfce6bbc78df8675b1747462b1ec1c74b7d6f/figures/issue_654/gap_per_tier_blog.png)

> **Figure.** *Context persistence is largest at the input and decays with depth.* Gap above 0 = query-end state closer to its OWN context than a random one. Shuffled-pair floor half-band ~0.003–0.03 across layers. Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct, 810 pairs.

- Centered cosine falls **0.60 (L0) → 0.16 (L7) → 0.14 (L14) → 0.11 (L21) → 0.088 (L27)** — a monotone-ish decay matching the ICL "task vector computed early, applied late" picture (2310.15916).
- The decay never reaches the floor (final-layer gap still 14.5× the band): context is *attenuated*, not *erased*, by query integration.
- Both read positions are a structural ChatML `\n` delimiter, so early-layer *magnitudes* partly reflect shared format signal — the depth *shape* is the load-bearing read, not the absolute level.

### A confound-free same-slot read confirms the query never dominates (companion)

The two-position read compares two *different* tokens, so part of its similarity is token identity. The companion read fixes that: residual at the *same* fixed generation slot, context-only vs context+query — the only difference is the query's presence.

![Same-slot cosine (context-only vs context+query) per layer per tier; tightly clustered curves decaying from ~0.99 to ~0.64–0.71](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/superkaiba/explore-persona-space/92ddfce6bbc78df8675b1747462b1ec1c74b7d6f/figures/issue_654/companion_blog.png)

> **Figure.** *Adding the query never displaces the generation-slot readout below ~0.64 cosine.* Cosine of the context-only vs context+query residual at the fixed assistant-generation slot, per tier. Confound-free (same position). Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct, 810 pairs.

- The readout is **0.99 at layer 0** (the query barely registers early), bottoms at **0.66 at layer 23**, ends **0.68 at layer 27** — even at the deepest layer a full user turn moves the state by at most ~1/3.
- The four tiers cluster within ~0.07 at every depth: once the structural confound is removed, context type barely modulates query displacement.

### Per-pair alignment decays but whole-bank geometry converges late (a DV divergence)

Centered cosine is a per-pair read; linear CKA asks the bank-level question — does the context bank's *geometry* survive into the query bank. The two disagree informatively.

![Per-pair centered cosine (solid, decaying) vs whole-bank linear CKA (dashed, rising late) vs shuffled-bank CKA floor (flat near zero), per layer](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/superkaiba/explore-persona-space/92ddfce6bbc78df8675b1747462b1ec1c74b7d6f/figures/issue_654/cosine_vs_cka_blog.png)

> **Figure.** *Per-pair alignment decays with depth; whole-bank geometry instead converges late.* Per-pair centered cosine (solid) vs linear CKA between the context bank and query bank (dashed) vs shuffled-bank CKA floor (dotted, ~0.01). All 810 pairs, Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct.

- CKA dips to **0.29 at layer 7** then *rises* to **0.76 at layer 27** (shuffled-bank floor ~0.01) — the opposite trajectory to per-pair cosine's late decay.
- Reading: late layers push every context toward a shared task/format subspace, so the *banks* grow geometrically alike (high CKA) while *individual* pairs drift (low cosine). This is the cleanest sign that the late last-token state is dominated by generic generation structure — and why H3 is weak: late geometry is shared across tiers by construction.

## Data

The battery is **81 contexts × 10 queries = 810 pairs** over four context tiers, each context paired against the same fixed 10-query bank so query type is a clean within-bank factor. ## Interpretation Critique — Round 1

**Verdict: REVISE**

The data is solid and the dual-position contract is intact (verified at the tensor level). The headline framing, however, leans on the wrong floor and smooths over two confounds the construct was supposed to rule out — query length and the cross-tier-vs-within-tier floor distinction. The companion read and the CKA divergence are the honest, well-supported parts of the writeup.

### Overclaims

- **"6.2–25× above the shuffled floor at every layer" (Takeaway 1, headline title, Finding 1).** This multiple is computed against the **GLOBAL (cross-tier) floor**, which sits at ~0.00 (`global.shuffled_floor.mean` ≈ −0.002 to +0.003 at all layers; `issue654_analyze.py:322-324` deranges over all 810 indices). But the construct ("is the query-end state closer to ITS OWN context than to a random one") is properly tested against the **within-tier** floor — which is what the hero figure actually plots. Against the within-tier floor the multiples are far smaller, and for the persona tier they collapse: persona L7 gap = 0.018 = **2.0× the within-tier half-band**, L8 = 0.013 = ~1.7×, not 6–25×. The cross-tier floor is artificially low because persona/generic/ICL/wildchat have different mean directions, so a cross-tier shuffle measures "is it the same KIND of context," not "is it the same context." Headline overclaims the effect size by citing the easier floor while the figure shows the harder one. — Suggested fix: state the multiple against the **within-tier** floor (the construct-valid baseline) and report the per-tier range honestly, with persona called out as the weakest (2–3× the band mid-stack). The H2-rejection claim survives for generic/ICL/wildchat; for persona it is marginal mid-stack.

- **"Context type separates only at layer 0 (a prompt-structure confound)" (Takeaway 5).** False as stated. Against each tier's own within-tier floor, the four tiers separate substantially through ~L8 (spread 0.50 at L0, 0.16 at L6, 0.10 at L8) and persona is the LOWEST-gap (least persistent) tier in **21 of 28 layers**, wildchat the highest early. The "within ~0.07" clustering is the COMPANION read (a different DV), not the per-pair gap. — Suggested fix: separate the two DVs explicitly. Say the per-pair within-tier gap shows a consistent ordering (persona lowest, wildchat highest) through mid-stack — which is the OPPOSITE of the plan's H3 prediction ("persona persists MORE") — and that the same-slot companion read collapses tier differences to ~0.07. Don't conflate them.

- **"the matched gap above it runs 25× the floor half-band at layer 0 down to a minimum 6.2× at layer 26" (Finding 1).** The true MAX multiple against the global floor is 28.3× at L5, not 25× at L0; the body anchors on L0. Minor, but the "6.2–25×" range understates the top end. — Suggested fix: "6.2× (L26) to 28× (L5)" or just drop the upper bound precision.

### Surprising Unmentioned Patterns

- **Query LENGTH dominates the persona early-layer signal — a large, unmentioned confound.** `per_context_type.persona[L].by_query_type`: at L0 short queries give matched cosine 0.80–0.82 while long queries give 0.01–0.08 — an ~0.8 swing purely on query length, with topicality near-irrelevant. At L7 the off-topic-long persona cell is even **negative** (−0.072). The early-layer persona "persistence" the headline celebrates is, for that tier, largely a length artifact: short queries place the query-end `\n` few tokens after the context-end `\n`, so the two residuals are mechanically closer. This is exactly the confound the construct should isolate, and the tier-averaged hero figure hides it. The generic tier shows much weaker length dependence (0.56–0.60 across all four query cells at L0), which makes the persona behavior more striking, not less. — Where: `eval_results/issue_654/per_layer_displacement.json` → `per_context_type.persona.{0,7}.by_query_type`. Why it matters: it reframes "context persists early" as partly "short queries don't move the read token far."

- **Persona is the weakest tier, not a wash.** As above — 21/28 layers lowest within-tier gap. The body's "H3 weak" understates a clean, monotone-in-direction ordering that contradicts the plan's H3 sign. That's a finding, not a null.

- **Raw cosine craters at the final layer (L27): 0.64 → 0.38.** `global.raw_cos_mean[26]=0.635 → [27]=0.383`. Centered cosine doesn't show this (it bumps up to 0.088). The final layer behaves differently (likely unembedding-aligned norm reallocation). Not load-bearing, but an honest "raw cosine anomaly at L27" footnote would be appropriate given the anisotropy caveat is already in play.

# Matched delimiter-position residual cosine sits above the within-tier shuffled floor at every layer of Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct, but query length dominates the persona tier (MODERATE confidence)

<!-- clean-result-v3 -->

## Takeaways

- The query-end residual stays closer to its **own** context than a deranged one at every layer (single seed). H2 ("no persistence") is rejected for 3 tiers; **marginal** for persona.
- **Query length, not context type, drives the persona layer-0 signal:** short queries score 0.81, long 0.05 (0.76 gap); other tiers move under 0.10 by length.
- The plan's H3 ("persona persists most") is **rejected in the opposite direction** — persona is the LOWEST-persisting tier in **21 of 28 layers**.
- The same-slot companion read (different-token confound removed; length/position confounds remain) holds the generation-slot state at **0.63-0.72 cosine** in late layers — consistent with context persistence, not proof of it.
- Read position is the last-prompt token, the known-weak persona-content proxy (Persona Vectors 2507.21509); residual geometry, not a behavioral claim.

## What I ran

- **Why:** A recurring question in this project's persona line is *where* in the stack the model stops tracking its context and starts answering the query. Prior work read one position per prompt for family clustering ([#594](https://eps.superkaiba.com/tasks/594)) or role-vs-persona separation ([#634](https://eps.superkaiba.com/tasks/634)); none contrasted the context-end and query-end positions within one prompt. This run measures that displacement per layer.
- **Design:** One manipulated axis — **read position** (context-span-end vs query-span-end token) — crossed with context type (4 tiers) × query type (on/off-topic × short/long). 81 contexts × 10 queries = 810 pairs, one forward pass each, residuals at all 28 layers. Single seed (42).
- **Training:** none — forward-pass measurement on base `Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct` (bf16, `output_hidden_states=True`, ChatML).
- **Eval:** per-layer per-pair **centered cosine** (global-mean-centered, anisotropy-robust DV) between the two positions; a **shuffled-pair derangement floor** (B=1000) computed both globally and **within each tier**; **whole-bank linear CKA** as a secondary geometry read; and a **companion same-position contrast** (context-only vs context+query at the fixed generation slot) that removes the different-token confound. No judge, no generation.

## Findings

### Matched cosine sits above the within-tier floor at every layer — H2 rejected, but marginal for persona

The construct-valid baseline is the **within-tier** shuffled floor (derange query↔context within a tier). The global cross-tier floor sits near zero only because the four tiers differ in mean direction. The within-tier floors are NOT near zero, and against them the multiples are modest.

![Matched centered cosine per tier vs layer; each tier's within-tier shuffled floor shaded, none near zero, matched curves above their own band at every depth](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/superkaiba/explore-persona-space/994feb766d4cce377032697b269ca823029d631a/figures/issue_654/hero_displacement_blog.png)

> **Figure.** *Matched query-end cosine stays above its own-tier shuffled floor at every layer.* Solid = matched-pair centered cosine; shaded = that tier's within-tier shuffled floor (2.5/97.5 pctile, B=1000) — NOT near zero (persona 0.43, generic/ICL 0.25 at layer 0). Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct, 810 pairs.

- Generic / ICL / real-chat clear their floor band by 4-12× at L0 and 2.7-11.7× mid-stack — H2 decisively rejected.
- **Persona is marginal:** matched 0.50 vs floor 0.43 at L0 (3.2×), 2.0× the band at L7. Persona prompts are mutually similar, so the floor is high.

### Query length, not context type, dominates the persona layer-0 signal

The tier-averaged view hides a larger effect inside the persona tier: a near-1.0 swing by query length.

![Grouped bars: layer-0 matched cosine by query length per tier; persona short 0.81 vs long 0.05, other tiers nearly flat](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/superkaiba/explore-persona-space/994feb766d4cce377032697b269ca823029d631a/figures/issue_654/query_length_split_blog.png)

### Persona is the lowest-persisting tier — H3 rejected in the opposite direction

The plan predicted persona would persist *more* than the other tiers. The within-tier gap (matched − own floor) shows the reverse.

![Matched-minus-shuffled gap per layer per tier; persona lowest at almost every depth, decaying from layer 0](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/superkaiba/explore-persona-space/994feb766d4cce377032697b269ca823029d631a/figures/issue_654/gap_per_tier_blog.png)

### Same-slot read holds the generation-slot state at 0.63-0.72 cosine in late layers

The two-position read compares two different `\n` tokens, so part of its similarity is token identity. The companion read fixes the slot — same generation position, context-only vs context+query — removing the different-token confound. Length / position / extra-turn confounds remain (no length-matched dummy-query control).

![Same-slot cosine per layer per tier; curves start near 0.99, bottom around 0.63-0.72 in late layers, cluster within ~0.07](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/superkaiba/explore-persona-space/994feb766d4cce377032697b269ca823029d631a/figures/issue_654/companion_blog.png)

Centered cosine is a per-pair read; linear CKA asks whether the context bank's geometry survives into the query bank. The two diverge.

![Per-pair centered cosine (solid, decaying) vs whole-bank CKA (dashed, dipping mid-stack then rising late) vs shuffled-bank CKA floor near 0.01](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/superkaiba/explore-persona-space/994feb766d4cce377032697b269ca823029d631a/figures/issue_654/cosine_vs_cka_blog.png)

# Matched delimiter-position residual cosine sits above the within-tier shuffled floor at every layer of Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct, but query length dominates the persona tier (MODERATE confidence)

<!-- clean-result-v3 -->

## Takeaways

- The query-end residual stays closer to its **own** context than a deranged one at every layer (single seed). H2 ("no persistence") is rejected for 3 tiers; **marginal** for persona.
- **Query length, not context type, drives the persona layer-0 signal:** short queries score 0.81, long 0.05 (0.76 gap); other tiers move under 0.10 by length.
- The plan's H3 ("persona persists most") is **rejected in the opposite direction** — persona is the LOWEST-persisting tier in **21 of 28 layers**.
- The same-slot companion read (different-token confound removed; length/position confounds remain) holds the generation-slot state at **0.63-0.72 cosine** in late layers — consistent with context persistence, not proof of it.
- Read position is the last-prompt token, the known-weak persona-content proxy (Persona Vectors 2507.21509); residual geometry, not a behavioral claim.

## What I ran

- **Why:** A recurring question in this project's persona line is *where* in the stack the model stops tracking its context and starts answering the query. Prior work read one position per prompt for family clustering ([#594](https://eps.superkaiba.com/tasks/594)) or role-vs-persona separation ([#634](https://eps.superkaiba.com/tasks/634)); none contrasted the context-end and query-end positions within one prompt. This run measures that displacement per layer.
- **Design:** One manipulated axis — **read position** (context-span-end vs query-span-end token) — crossed with context type (4 tiers) × query type (on/off-topic × short/long). 81 contexts × 10 queries = 810 pairs, one forward pass each, residuals at all 28 layers. Single seed (42).
- **Training:** none — forward-pass measurement on base `Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct` (bf16, `output_hidden_states=True`, ChatML).
- **Eval:** per-layer per-pair **centered cosine** (global-mean-centered, anisotropy-robust DV) between the two positions; a **shuffled-pair derangement floor** (B=1000) computed both globally and **within each tier**; **whole-bank linear CKA** as a secondary geometry read; and a **companion same-position contrast** (context-only vs context+query at the fixed generation slot) that removes the different-token confound. No judge, no generation.

## Findings

### Matched cosine sits above the within-tier floor at every layer — H2 rejected, but marginal for persona

The construct-valid baseline is the **within-tier** shuffled floor (derange query↔context within a tier). The global cross-tier floor sits near zero only because the four tiers differ in mean direction. The within-tier floors are NOT near zero, and against them the multiples are modest.

![Matched centered cosine per tier vs layer; each tier's within-tier shuffled floor shaded, none near zero, matched curves above their own band at every depth](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/superkaiba/explore-persona-space/994feb766d4cce377032697b269ca823029d631a/figures/issue_654/hero_displacement_blog.png)

> **Figure.** *Matched query-end cosine stays above its own-tier shuffled floor at every layer.* Solid = matched-pair centered cosine; shaded = that tier's within-tier shuffled floor (2.5/97.5 pctile, B=1000) — NOT near zero (persona 0.43, generic/ICL 0.25 at layer 0). Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct, 810 pairs.

- Generic / ICL / real-chat clear their floor band by 10-16× at L0 (real-chat highest) and 4.5-10.5× through mid-stack (L10-18) — H2 decisively rejected.
- **Persona is marginal:** matched 0.50 vs floor 0.43 at L0 (3.2×), 2.0× the band at L7. Persona prompts are mutually similar, so the floor is high.

### Query length, not context type, dominates the persona layer-0 signal

The tier-averaged view hides a larger effect inside the persona tier: a large 0.76 short-vs-long gap by query length.

![Grouped bars: layer-0 matched cosine by query length per tier; persona short 0.81 vs long 0.05, other tiers nearly flat](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/superkaiba/explore-persona-space/994feb766d4cce377032697b269ca823029d631a/figures/issue_654/query_length_split_blog.png)

> **Figure.** *Query length drives the persona layer-0 signal; persona is the length-sensitive outlier.* Layer-0 matched centered cosine, short vs long query, per tier. Persona: short 0.81, long 0.05 (0.76 gap); outside persona, the other tiers move under 0.10 by length. Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct, 810 pairs.

- Persona short-vs-long split stays 0.30-0.76 through layers 0-11; the off-topic-long persona cell goes **negative** at L7-L8 (−0.072, −0.085).
- Short queries place the query-end `\n` few tokens after the context-end `\n`, so the residuals are mechanically close. This is why the same-slot companion read is the load-bearing persistence evidence, not these two-position numbers.

### Persona is the lowest-persisting tier — H3 rejected in the opposite direction

The plan predicted persona would persist *more* than the other tiers. The within-tier gap (matched − own floor) shows the reverse.

![Matched-minus-shuffled gap per layer per tier; persona lowest at almost every depth, decaying from layer 0](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/superkaiba/explore-persona-space/994feb766d4cce377032697b269ca823029d631a/figures/issue_654/gap_per_tier_blog.png)

> **Figure.** *Persona is the lowest-persisting tier at almost every depth — opposite to the H3 prediction.* Gap = matched − own-tier shuffled centered cosine per layer. Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct, 810 pairs.

- Persona is the lowest-gap tier in **21 of 28 layers**. At L7: generic 0.129, real-chat 0.110, ICL 0.049, persona 0.018.
- This corroborates the plan's flagged caveat (Persona Vectors 2507.21509): the last-prompt-token read is the *weakest* for persona content, so a low persona signal is expected, not a null.

### Same-slot read holds the generation-slot state at 0.63-0.72 cosine in late layers

The two-position read compares two different `\n` tokens, so part of its similarity is token identity. The companion read fixes the slot — same generation position, context-only vs context+query — removing the different-token confound. Length / position / extra-turn confounds remain (no length-matched dummy-query control).

![Same-slot cosine per layer per tier; curves start near 0.99, bottom around 0.63-0.72 in late layers, cluster within ~0.07](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/superkaiba/explore-persona-space/994feb766d4cce377032697b269ca823029d631a/figures/issue_654/companion_blog.png)

> **Figure.** *Adding the query holds the generation-slot readout at 0.63-0.72 cosine in late layers.* Context-only vs context+query at the fixed generation slot, per tier. Removes the different-token confound; length/position confounds remain. Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct, 810 pairs.

- Mean-of-tiers minimum **0.665** (L23); per-tier minima reach **0.629** (generic, L23), wildchat ends 0.640. Tiers cluster within ~0.07 at every depth.
- This is the confound-robust evidence consistent with context persistence. Cosine is not a linear displacement fraction, so I report the value, not a "fraction moved."

### Per-pair alignment decays with depth while whole-bank CKA dips then rises

Centered cosine is a per-pair read; linear CKA asks whether the context bank's geometry survives into the query bank. The two diverge.

![Per-pair centered cosine (solid, decaying) vs whole-bank CKA (dashed, dipping mid-stack then rising late) vs shuffled-bank CKA floor near 0.01](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/superkaiba/explore-persona-space/994feb766d4cce377032697b269ca823029d631a/figures/issue_654/cosine_vs_cka_blog.png)

> **Figure.** *Per-pair alignment decays; whole-bank CKA dips mid-stack then rises late.* Per-pair centered cosine (solid) vs context-bank↔query-bank linear CKA (dashed) vs shuffled-bank CKA floor (dotted, ~0.01). Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct, 810 pairs.

- CKA is **0.53 (L0), 0.63 (L5)**, dips to a **trough of 0.29 (L7)**, then rises to **0.76 (L27)** — a mid-stack dip plus late rise, not simple late convergence.
- Descriptive geometry, not a mechanism: the late rise is consistent with a shared last-token / format subspace. Footnote: raw (uncentered) cosine craters at the final layer (0.64 at L26 → 0.38 at L27), likely norm reallocation; the centered DV does not.

## Data

n/a — no training in this task. Forward-pass-only measurement on the base model.

### Evaluated with

The battery is **81 contexts × 10 queries = 810 pairs** over four context tiers, each context paired against the same fixed 10-query bank so query type is a clean within-bank factor. Identity: persona system prompts (11 = 10 curated personas + the default assistant), generic instructions (20 UltraChat first-user prompts), in-context example blocks (20 held-out 4-exchange UltraChat Q/A blocks), real chat turns (30 WildChat conversation prefixes). Both read positions decode to `\n` in all 810 pairs — expected for ChatML, and why centered cosine + the same-slot companion read are the load-bearing DVs rather than raw cosine.

### 1. Length-matched dummy-query control for the same-slot companion read — [Type: Diagnostic]

**Parent:** #654
**question_relation:** same
**followup_label:** length-matched-dummy-query-control
**Goal:** Measure, per layer in Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct, how much appending a user query displaces the last-token residual-stream state away from the context-established state (centered cosine + CKA + shuffled-pair floor) across persona / generic-instruction / ICL / wild-chat contexts and varied queries, to characterize context-dominant vs query-dominant layer regimes.
**Hypothesis:** The late-layer companion-read cosine of 0.63-0.72 (Finding 4) reflects QUERY CONTENT, not the mechanical length/position offset the body flags as an unresolved confound. A content-free dummy query of matched token length (e.g. a fixed neutral filler turn padded to each real query's length) will hold the same-slot cosine substantially HIGHER than the real-content query — the content-driven displacement is the gap between the two curves.
**Falsification:** If the dummy-query companion cosine sits within ~0.03 of the real-query companion cosine at every layer, the late-layer companion displacement is a length/position artifact, not query-content integration — and Finding 4's "consistent with context persistence" read weakens to "consistent with mechanical token offset." Either outcome rewrites the Takeaways bullet on the companion read.
**Differs from parent:** Adds ONE new query arm — a content-neutral dummy query padded to each real query's token length — extracted at the same three slots; everything else (model, contexts, read positions, metrics, seed) identical.

**Pre-filled spec (from parent):**
- Model: same — `Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct`, bf16, `output_hidden_states=True`, ChatML.
- Data: same 81-context battery; the 10-query bank EXTENDED with a matched set of content-neutral dummy queries (one per real query, padded to the same token length with a fixed neutral filler), frozen in `battery.json` meta.
- Seeds: same — 42 (single seed; this round isolates the confound, not seed variance).
- Eval: same — centered cosine + within-tier B=1000 derangement floor + companion same-slot contrast (`scripts/issue654_analyze.py`); the new read is the dummy-vs-real companion-curve gap per layer.
- Config: same as parent EXCEPT one added query arm (length-matched dummy queries) → ~81 extra context-only-reusable forwards + the new pair forwards (~810 → the dummy arm reuses the 81 cached context-only `.pt` banks, so only the dummy pairs re-extract).

**Estimated cost:** ~0.5 GPU-hours on 1× A100-80 (GCP `a2-ultragpu-1g`, `lora-7b` intent) — same envelope as the parent's 0.4 GPU-h, dummy arm is a fraction of the 810-pair battery; CPU metric phase off-pod.
**If it works:** The companion read's persistence claim is confound-controlled — the body's single largest open caveat (Finding 4: "length/position/extra-turn confounds remain; no length-matched dummy-query control") is resolved, lifting confidence on the persistence headline.
**If it fails:** The late-layer companion cosine is a mechanical artifact; Finding 4 is reframed and the persistence headline is appropriately demoted — a record-correcting result.
